Nothing was built, applied, moved or deleted; no raw image was opened (capture times come from existing receipts and protocols).

station.name: GFI Florida weather station (Geophysical Institute, University of Bergen), Bergen
station.data_portal: https://veret.gfi.uib.no/?action=period_query (as named in the benchmark analysis scripts; not contacted for this manifest)
station.sensor_height_m: about 45 m a.s.l., roof-mounted (N196, N198; GFI and UiB pages, terrain models)
station.quantity: Lufttrykk = station-level air pressure in hPa, NOT reduced to sea level (N196: GFI's page says not adjusted; N198: file minus SYNOP sea-level pressure -6.85 hPa (SD 0.25), file minus SYNOP station pressure -2.47 hPa (SD 0.20), Sep 2022-May 2023). Mean of all valid 2020-2023 values here: 1004.3 hPa.

evidence_earlier: N196: all 10 genuine operator website readings match the export at local time minus the UTC offset; the 15 Jan 2022 Hunga Tonga wave fits only UTC.
N198: all 9 operator readings of FF_UM runs 6-20 match at local minus the UTC offset and none at local; hourly lag scans against the UTC SYNOP are smallest at lag 0 in summer and winter.
evidence_this_manifest: DST signature: on every last Sunday of March (2020-2023) the 02:xx hour is absent and 03:xx occurs twice in a smooth, monotone row sequence (the first 03:xx block is UTC 02:xx); on every last Sunday of October there is no gap and no duplicate. A civil-local-time export would have no duplicate in March and a doubled 02:xx in October.

Semidiurnal tide (S2) fitted to the 2020-2023 series: stamp time of the maximum 10:29 in CET periods and 10:13 in CEST periods (amplitude about 0.19 hPa). The sun-locked tide does not move by the +60 min a civil-time stamp would show in summer.

Hunga Tonga Lamb wave on 15 Jan 2022: rise from about 18:10-18:20, peak 18:30, sharp fall 18:40-18:50 (stamp). Great-circle distance 15585 km; eruption 04:14:45 UTC; that is about 304-310 m/s if the stamps are UTC (reported Lamb-wave speeds about 310-320 m/s) but about 327-333 m/s if they were CET. The antipodal pass at 01:50-02:40 stamp on 16 Jan also fits UTC.
time_base.conversion: image clocks -> UTC per series (see runs); station stamps are used as UTC directly

missing_value_markers: 59 fully blank trailing rows in the FF_BM-period export (as many as its absent stamps; there the 14-15 Dec 2021 outage stamps are absent, not 9999.99)
quirks: Spring-forward Sundays (2020-03-29, 2021-03-28, 2022-03-27, 2023-03-26): 02:xx absent, 03:xx twice; relabel the first 03:xx block as 02:xx (row order). No FF_AC/FF_RE/FF_BM imaging period touches these days.
Off-grid stamps: 2021-09-10 05:29 and 2021-12-18 07:29 (2021 export; the 07:29 one lies inside FF_BM c3); many :x1-:x3 stamps in Ambient_Florida.xlsx from Feb 2023.

2023 export: header row has 7 cells (4 empty); two hand-entered numbers in column 4 on 2023-05-12 20:20 (1020.7) and 2023-05-13 02:20 (1020.4) where Lufttrykk is 9999.99. Not station data (N198); inside ac51 (excluded run).
Whole-number pressures are stored as integer cells (e.g. 1018); read them as float.
Consecutive yearly exports overlap by one day (1 Jan 00:00-23:50 of the next year) with identical values (144 of 144 stamps).
